paragraphs.title: The Model of Jerusalem Under Siege

easy.explanation: The LORD told Ezekiel to take a tile and portray Jerusalem upon it.
easy.q: What was Ezekiel told to take and portray Jerusalem upon?

answers: A fort and a siege mount
easy.explanation: He was told to build a fort and cast up a mount against the city.
easy.q: What was Ezekiel told to build against the city?

easy.explanation: The iron pan was set as a wall between Ezekiel and the city.
easy.q: What was set between Ezekiel and the city?

answers: A fort, a mount, camps, and battering rams
A tile, a pan, and an uncovered arm
medium.explanation: The verses mention a fort, a mount, a camp, and battering rams around the city.
medium.q: Which group lists the siege actions described in these verses?

medium.explanation: A battering ram was a siege device used to attack a city's defenses.
medium.q: What is a battering ram used for in the context of a siege?

answers: A hard barrier between Ezekiel and the city
medium.explanation: The iron pan formed a wall between Ezekiel and Jerusalem during the siege.
medium.q: What did the iron pan represent in the sign?

answers: To portray the coming siege visibly
To measure the height of the wall
challenge.explanation: The model acted as a visible sign of the siege that would come upon Jerusalem.
challenge.q: Why was Ezekiel commanded to make a model of Jerusalem instead of merely speaking about it?

answers: The prophet was about to enter the city
There was a strong barrier between the prophet and the city
The city was protected from siege
challenge.explanation: The iron pan symbolized a firm barrier and the city's siege.
challenge.q: What can be understood from setting the iron pan between Ezekiel and the city?

answers: They all describe the prophet's journey
They all portray Jerusalem under siege
challenge.explanation: Together, these signs present a symbolic picture of besieged Jerusalem.
challenge.q: How do the tile, the siege actions, and the iron pan express one central idea?

paragraphs.title: Bearing Iniquity in a Forced Position

easy.explanation: Ezekiel was first commanded to lie upon his left side.
easy.q: Upon which side was Ezekiel first told to lie?

easy.explanation: After completing the first period, he was told to lie upon his right side.
easy.q: Upon which side was Ezekiel told to lie afterward?

answers: The house of Israel and the house of Judah
easy.explanation: The days represented the iniquity of Israel and then the iniquity of Judah.
easy.q: Whose iniquity was represented by the days Ezekiel lay on his sides?

medium.explanation: The appointed days represented the years of the people's iniquity.
medium.q: What did the number of days Ezekiel lay on his side represent?

answers: I will bind or restrain thee
I will build camps around thee
medium.explanation: Bands signify restraint, limiting Ezekiel's ability to move.
medium.q: What does the phrase “I will lay bands upon thee” mean in this passage?

answers: Turn continually from side to side
medium.explanation: He was not to turn from one side to another until the siege days were completed.
medium.q: What was Ezekiel required to do while facing the siege?

answers: It represented bearing iniquity and prolonged suffering
It represented preparation for a journey
challenge.explanation: The long, restricted posture visibly represented bearing the people's iniquity.
challenge.q: How did Ezekiel's forced position express his prophetic role?

answers: The prophecy had two stages concerning Israel and Judah
The prophet moved the city to another place
challenge.explanation: The two positions corresponded to the iniquity of Israel and then Judah.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the change from the left side to the right side?

answers: The restraint continued until the appointed period was complete
The restraint was meant to make the prophet comfortable
The restraint made the number of days meaningless
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel remained restrained until he had ended the appointed days of the siege.
challenge.q: What was the connection between Ezekiel's inability to turn and the siege days?

paragraphs.title: Bread and Water During Siege and Defilement

answers: A mixture of grains and legumes
easy.explanation: He was told to use wheat, barley, beans, lentiles, millet, and fitches.
easy.q: What ingredients was Ezekiel told to use in making the bread?

easy.explanation: The LORD said that his meat would be eaten by weight.
easy.q: How was Ezekiel's bread to be eaten?

answers: Dung that came out of man
easy.explanation: He was first told to bake the bread with human dung.
easy.q: What was Ezekiel first told to use for baking the bread?

answers: He would drink water without limit
He would drink a measured amount of water
Water would be poured over the bread
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that his water would be carefully measured and limited.
medium.q: What does “thou shalt drink also water by measure” mean?

answers: He was concerned about ceremonial defilement
He wanted to prepare different bread
medium.explanation: Ezekiel said that his soul had not been polluted and that he had not eaten unclean meat.
medium.q: Why did Ezekiel object to using human dung?

answers: He replaced the human dung with cow's dung
medium.explanation: The LORD allowed Ezekiel to use cow's dung instead of human dung.
medium.q: What did the LORD do after Ezekiel objected?

answers: They portrayed limited and carefully measured eating and drinking
They portrayed an abundance of food
They portrayed the end of prophecy
challenge.explanation: The measured portions and unusual bread portrayed scarcity during a siege.
challenge.q: How did the restrictions on food and water portray siege conditions?

answers: The sign involved hardship, including a concern about purity
The command described a joyful feast
The command did not involve making bread
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel accepted the prophetic sign but objected to the proposed method because of purity concerns.
challenge.q: What can be learned from Ezekiel's response to the command?

answers: It portrayed simple, restricted food during siege
It showed that the people were eating a festive meal
It indicated the number of siege camps
challenge.explanation: The mixed ingredients, measured amount, and restricted preparation together portrayed hardship and scarcity.
challenge.q: Why was the bread made from a mixture of different ingredients?

paragraphs.title: Scarcity, Anxiety, and Decline in Jerusalem

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem.”
easy.q: What did the LORD say He would break in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: They would eat bread by weight and with care.
easy.q: How would the people of Jerusalem eat their bread?

easy.explanation: They would drink water by measure and with astonishment.
easy.q: How would the people of Jerusalem drink their water?

answers: The breaking brought scarcity and rationing
medium.explanation: When the staff of bread was broken, food became scarce and had to be rationed.
medium.q: What was the connection between breaking the staff of bread and eating by weight?

medium.explanation: The people would eat with care and drink with astonishment.
medium.q: What emotional condition accompanied the scarcity?

answers: They would be astonished and consume away for their iniquity
medium.explanation: The scarcity would bring astonishment and cause them to consume away for their iniquity.
medium.q: What would scarcity cause among the people of the city?

answers: They show that the actions symbolized scarcity and distress in Jerusalem
They cancel the meaning of the earlier actions
challenge.explanation: These verses explain that the symbolic actions represented hunger, thirst, and distress in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: How do these verses explain the meaning of Ezekiel's earlier actions?

answers: Scarcity is connected with the people's iniquity
Scarcity is described as a reward for iniquity
The verses make no connection between them
challenge.explanation: The passage ends by saying that the people would consume away for their iniquity.
challenge.q: What relationship do the verses show between scarcity and iniquity?

answers: Strict control of portions because of scarcity
challenge.explanation: Both expressions emphasize rationing and severe shortage.
challenge.q: What does the combination of bread by weight and water by measure emphasize?
